title: Degree-zero Boolean functions are constant
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of degree at most $0$; that is, every set
$S$ with nonzero Fourier--Walsh coefficient $\hat f(S)\ne 0$ satisfies $|S|\le 0$. Then
$f$ is constant: for every point $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ one has $f(x)=f(x_0)$, where $x_0$ is
the all-$\mathtt{false}$ point.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function on the n-dimensional hypercube
f has degree at most 0 (nonzero Fourier coefficients supported on sets of size at most 0)
replaced:
A Boolean function $f$ of degree at most $0$ is constant: $f(x) = f(\mathrm{default})$ for all
$x$.
